statement_en: We say $H$ is a unique subgraph of $G$ if there is exactly one way to find $H$ as a subgraph (not necessarily induced) of $G$. Is there a graph on $n$ vertices with\[\gg \frac{2^{\binom{n}{2}}}{n!}\]many distinct unique subgraphs?
statement_lean:
namespace SimpleGraph
variable {V : Type*}
def IsUniqueSubgraph (G H : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃! G' : SimpleGraph V, G' ≤ H ∧ Nonempty (G.Iso G')
end SimpleGraph

namespace SimpleGraph
variable {V : Type*}
noncomputable def uniqueSubgraphCount (H : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  {G : SimpleGraph V | G ≤ H ∧ IsUniqueSubgraph G H}.ncard
end SimpleGraph

open Filter SimpleGraph

theorem erdos_65644 :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin n),
      c * ((2 : ℝ) ^ n.choose 2 / n.factorial) ≤ (uniqueSubgraphCount H : ℝ) := by
  sorry
